name: Aircraft carrier
funFact: A Nimitz-class carrier has only 333 m to land a jet approaching at 240 km/h — pilots have about 5 seconds of runway. The arresting wire stops the aircraft in roughly 100 m, from 240 km/h to zero in 2 seconds — approximately the same g-force as a car crash. Pilots describe landing on a carrier at night as 'a controlled collision with a postage stamp.'

name: Amazon River
funFact: The Amazon River discharges more water into the ocean than the next seven largest rivers combined.

name: Ant
funFact: A single ant can carry 10–50 times its own body weight.

name: Arm span
description: Average adult arm span ≈ 1.8 m — roughly equal to your height.
funFact: Leonardo da Vinci's Vitruvian Man illustrated that arm span equals height in a perfectly proportioned body — a principle still used in forensic anthropology.

name: Average human
funFact: The average human height has increased by about 10 cm over the last 150 years, largely due to improvements in nutrition.

name: Banana
funFact: The average person eats around 100 bananas a year.
exampleMeme: That is a lot of bananas.

name: Basketball hoop
funFact: The 10 ft (3.048 m) hoop height has never changed since James Naismith nailed a peach basket to a balcony railing in 1891.
exampleMeme: Just high enough to humble you.

name: Big Ben tower
funFact: Big Ben is actually the name of the bell inside the tower, not the tower itself. The tower's official name is the Elizabeth Tower, renamed in 2012.

name: Blue whale
funFact: Blue whales are among the rarest animals on Earth — there are only around 10,000–25,000 left.

name: Boeing 747
funFact: The 747 was designed in only 18 months — Boeing engineers called it 'The Incredibles.' The distinctive upper-deck hump was originally designed for nose-loading cargo; the passenger lounge upstairs was a last-minute addition. At peak production in the 1970s, one 747 was completed every three days.

name: Bowling lane
description: Foul line to head pin ≈ 18.29 m.
funFact: Bowling lanes are coated in a thin layer of oil that affects how the ball curves — professional bowlers study the oil pattern before every game.

name: Burj Khalifa
funFact: The Burj Khalifa is so tall that you can watch the sunset from the base, take the elevator to the top, and watch it set again.

name: Bus
funFact: The 12-metre standard for city buses wasn't set by engineering — it was determined by the turning radius required to navigate most city intersections. City road geometry and bus length evolved together: a 12-metre bus can make the same turn as a 12-metre road curve radius. Change one and you'd have to change both.
exampleMeme: Long enough to miss your stop twice.

name: Car
funFact: The average car spends about 95% of its life parked — moving for only around 1 hour per day.

name: Chopstick
funFact: Chopsticks have been used in China for over 3,000 years.

name: Comet tail
description: Pinned to an average large comet tail (~0.1 AU).
funFact: A comet's tail always points away from the Sun regardless of the direction the comet is travelling — pushed by solar wind.

name: Credit card
funFact: Every credit card in the world is exactly 85.6 mm long — an ISO standard.

name: Door
funFact: Standard door height is 2.032 m (6 ft 8 in) — chosen so 99% of people can walk through.

name: Double-decker bus
description: Double-decker bus height ≈ 4.38 m (height, not length).
funFact: The iconic red double-decker London bus was introduced in 1956. Its colour became standardised partly to make it immediately recognisable in traffic.

name: Earth → Moon
funFact: The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at about 3.8 cm per year — roughly the same rate your fingernails grow.

name: Earth → Sun
funFact: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth. If the Sun disappeared, we wouldn't know for over 8 minutes.

name: Earth's circumference
funFact: Eratosthenes calculated the Earth's circumference in 240 BC using only the angle of shadows in two cities — he was accurate to within 2%.

name: Eiffel Tower
funFact: The Eiffel Tower was the tallest man-made structure on Earth for 41 years after it was built in 1889.

name: Empire State Building
description: Empire State Building height ≈ 443 m (roof height, no antenna).
funFact: The Empire State Building was constructed in just 410 days — about a floor per day — and was the world's tallest building for nearly 40 years.

name: Football field
description: American football field length ≈ 100 yards (91.44 m).
funFact: American football fields were standardised at 100 yards in 1912, but end zones weren't added until 1920 — which is why the total field is 120 yards. The 'red zone' (inside the 20-yard line) is a TV invention from the 1970s and doesn't appear in the official rulebook. Every inch of the field dimensions traces back to the furlong-based imperial chain.

name: Footlong sub
funFact: In 2013, a photo went viral of a Subway 'Footlong' measuring only 11 inches. The resulting class action lawsuit settled for $525,000, with Subway agreeing to actually measure sandwiches to 12 inches. The scandal revealed that 'Footlong' had quietly become a brand name rather than a length guarantee.

name: Fridge
funFact: The average household fridge runs continuously for around 10–15 years and is one of the few appliances left on 24/7.

name: Giraffe
funFact: A giraffe's neck alone is about 1.8 m — nearly as tall as an average human.

name: Golden Gate Bridge
description: Golden Gate Bridge total length = 2,737 m.
funFact: The Golden Gate Bridge's main cables contain 80,000 miles of wire — enough to circle the equator 3 times. Each cable is 92 cm in diameter and contains 27,572 individual wires bundled together. The bridge flexes up to 8 metres sideways in strong winds.

name: Grain of rice
description: Typical grain of rice length ≈ 6 mm.
funFact: Rice has been cultivated for over 10,000 years and currently feeds more than half the world's population.

name: Grain of sand
funFact: There are more grains of sand on Earth's beaches than stars in the observable universe — roughly 7.5 quintillion grains.

name: Great Wall of China
description: Great Wall total length ≈ 21,196 km (including branches).
funFact: Despite the popular myth, the Great Wall of China is not visible from space with the naked eye — it's too narrow relative to its length.

name: Guitar
description: Typical acoustic guitar length ≈ 1.016 m (40 in).
funFact: The acoustic guitar's modern form was standardised in the 1850s by Spanish luthier Antonio Torres Jurado, whose designs are still the basis for guitars today.

name: Human hair
funFact: Hair width varies by individual: Asian hair averages ~80 µm, European ~60 µm, African varies widely. The world record for longest hair is 5.6 metres, held by Xie Qiuping of China, who hadn't cut it since 1973. Human hair grows about 15 cm per year and is one of the few tissues that grows continuously without any biological limit.

name: LEGO minifigure
funFact: There are over 4 billion LEGO minifigures in existence — making them the world's largest population group. If LEGO minifigures were a country, they'd outnumber every real nation on Earth by a factor of 2.

name: Light-second
description: Distance light travels in 1 second ≈ 299,792 km.
funFact: Light from the Moon reaches Earth in about 1.28 seconds. During Apollo missions, the communication delay was clearly noticeable to listeners on Earth.

name: Light-year
description: Distance light travels in one year ≈ 9.46 trillion km.
funFact: The nearest star to Earth (Proxima Centauri) is 4.24 light-years away. At the speed of the New Horizons spacecraft, it would take 78,000 years to reach it.

name: London to Sydney
description: London to Sydney flight distance ≈ 16,993 km.
funFact: London to Sydney is one of the longest commercial flight routes in the world — the direct Qantas flight takes about 19–20 hours.

name: Manhattan block
funFact: Manhattan blocks are asymmetric by design: east-west 'short blocks' are ~80 m, north-south 'long blocks' are ~264 m. The 1811 Commissioner's Plan chose this ratio to maximise property frontage on avenues. A New Yorker saying 'two blocks' can mean a 2-minute walk or a 15-minute walk depending entirely on which direction.

name: Marathon
funFact: The odd 42.195 km was set at the 1908 London Olympics so the race could start at Windsor Castle and finish in front of the Royal Family's box at the stadium. That specific palace-to-royal-box distance became the world standard — one of history's best examples of royal convenience accidentally defining global sport.

name: Mount Everest
funFact: Mount Everest grows about 4 mm taller every year due to the Indian tectonic plate continuing to push into Asia.

name: New York to London
funFact: Concorde crossed the Atlantic in under 3.5 hours — a journey that takes 7–8 hours on a commercial flight today.

name: Newborn baby
funFact: A human newborn is remarkably undeveloped compared to other primates. A foal can walk within hours of birth; a chimp newborn is neurologically equivalent to a 9-month-old human. If humans were born as developmentally mature as a chimp, gestation would need to be 21 months — our large brains force us out early.

name: Nile River
funFact: The Nile flows through 11 countries and has sustained human civilisation for over 5,000 years — the same river that flooded to feed ancient Egypt.

name: Olympic pool
description: Standard Olympic swimming pool length = 50 m.
funFact: An Olympic pool holds about 2.5 million litres of water and takes roughly 2 days to fill.

name: Paperclip
funFact: The paperclip was patented in 1867, but the iconic double-loop design most people use today wasn't invented until around 1899.

name: Park bench
funFact: The world's longest park bench is in Grabow, Germany — stretching 85 metres and seating around 400 people.

name: Pencil
funFact: The average pencil can draw a line about 56 km long before running out.

name: Red blood cell
description: Typical red blood cell diameter ≈ 8 µm.
funFact: Red blood cells are so small that about 5 million fit in a single drop of blood.

name: School bus
description: Standard North American school bus ≈ 10.67 m.
funFact: The yellow colour of school buses is officially called 'National School Bus Glossy Yellow' and was chosen in 1939 because it's the fastest colour for the human eye to notice in peripheral vision — you can spot school bus yellow before any other colour on the road.
exampleMeme: The universal unit of 'about this long.'

name: Short pool
funFact: Short course pools (25 m) are used for most club and national competitions — only the Olympics and World Championships use the 50 m standard.
exampleMeme: Half an Olympic pool, still exhausting.

name: Smartphone
funFact: The average person checks their phone around 96 times a day — roughly once every 10 minutes of waking life.

name: Spider silk
description: Diameter of a spider silk thread ≈ 3 µm.
funFact: Spider silk is stronger than steel by weight — a strand as thick as a pencil could stop a plane in flight.

name: Statue of Liberty
description: Statue of Liberty total height ≈ 93 m (base to torch).
funFact: Lady Liberty's index finger is 2.44 m long — roughly the height of a door — and her waist measures 10.7 m around.

name: Subway car
funFact: The New York City subway has 472 stations — more than any other metro system in the world — served by cars very similar in length to this.

name: Suitcase
funFact: The maximum checked baggage size on most airlines adds up to 158 cm (length + width + height) — a rule that dates back to the 1970s.

name: Swimming pool depth
funFact: Olympic pools must be exactly 2 m deep — shallow enough to see the bottom, deep enough to prevent wave reflection from slowing swimmers.

name: Telephone pole
funFact: There are around 180 million telephone poles in the US alone — enough to circle the Earth more than 7 times if laid end to end.

name: Tennis court
funFact: Tennis was first played on grass at Wimbledon in 1877. The first tournament had just 22 players and one umpire.

name: Toothbrush
funFact: The modern nylon-bristle toothbrush was invented in 1938. Before that, people used twigs, feathers, and animal hair.

name: Width of Australia
funFact: Australia is wider than the Moon. The Moon's diameter is about 3,474 km — Australia spans roughly 4,000 km east to west.

name: Wine bottle
funFact: The standard 750 ml wine bottle size was set in the 1970s — it was chosen partly because it matched the lung capacity of a glassblower.

name: Yoga mat
description: Standard yoga mat length ≈ 1.83 m (6 ft).
funFact: The yoga mat was invented in 1984 — yoga itself is 3,000 years old and was historically practiced on grass, stone, and animal skins. Angela Farmer created the first sticky mat from carpet underlay she found in her luggage while teaching in Germany. Before mass production, the standard yoga mat was a folded wool blanket.
